summary: Add a local LLM bridge integration to AppForge-LLM v4 so the current Vue/FastAPI web app can configure external model providers and run pipeline stages through an llm-bridge driver.
problem: AppForge-LLM v4 previously depended on local coding-agent CLIs or a generic command driver. The current app needed the interrupted LLM bridge work completed so users can configure API-key based providers in the web UI, select an active model, and have the backend expose a driver/readiness path that can use that provider through the local bridge.
target_users: Local AppForge-LLM v4 users who want to run app-generation stages with an external LLM provider instead of only Codex or Claude CLI
Developers maintaining the AppForge-LLM v4 FastAPI/Vue app and its pipeline runner
Operators running the local web server and local llm_bridge service
desired_outcomes: The web UI exposes a provider settings flow for storing API keys, selecting default models, testing provider connectivity, and activating the model used by AppForge.
The FastAPI server proxies provider management to a same-origin /api/llm surface and reports truthful readiness for APPFORGE_DRIVER=llm-bridge.
The pipeline runner can create an llm-bridge driver that calls the local bridge for stage generation.
The bridge service supports provider listing, model listing, provider upsert/delete, active model selection, health, test, generate, and stream endpoints.
The implementation is covered by backend web tests, bridge typecheck, frontend typecheck, frontend production build, and the existing Python test suite.
constraints: Keep the integration local-first; no deployment, publishing, or remote infrastructure provisioning is in scope.
Do not commit API keys or display stored secrets back in the browser.
Preserve existing Codex, Claude, generic, and auto driver behavior.
Reuse the repository's Vue/FastAPI/AppForge patterns rather than replacing the app shell.
Use the local llm_bridge service as the provider boundary; the browser must stay same-origin through FastAPI proxy endpoints.
assumptions: Provider credentials are supplied by local environment variables or by the local bridge config file, not by source-controlled files.
A single-shot llm-bridge driver is acceptable for stage text generation; fully agentic file-editing stages still need a CLI driver.
The bridge can be started separately from the web server with Bun using the llm_bridge package.
Routine ambiguity in the user's phrase '그것' maps to the interrupted LLM bridge/provider-settings implementation visible in the worktree.
non_goals: Do not deploy the web app or bridge service.
Do not add billing, account management, team sharing, OAuth, or hosted secret storage.
Do not replace the existing AppForge stage runner or checkpoint architecture.
Do not guarantee live provider calls without user-supplied credentials.
Do not broaden the feature into a general multi-agent orchestration system.
open_questions: Which provider/model the user will ultimately activate is left to runtime configuration; the safe default is to expose supported providers and require a configured active provider before reporting readiness.
Whether llm-bridge should become part of a one-command launcher remains outside this slice; the safe default is documented separate startup.
